## Why this notebook exists

Most causal tooling splits **graph identification**, **structural simulation**, **targeted estimation**, **DAG figures**, and **Bayesian heads** across languages or packages that do not share types. This stack keeps those steps in one Julia process with a typed hand-off (`IdentificationResult` / certificates → LMTP or mediation grids → DAGMakie → optional Turing or RxInfer).

Capability matrix:
[ECOSYSTEM_COMPARISON.md](https://github.com/SimonAB/CausalTargeted.jl/blob/main/ECOSYSTEM_COMPARISON.md).
Package `test/` remains the merge gate; the full CI matrix lives in
[causal-dynamics-book/scripts/stress_harness](https://github.com/SimonAB/causal-dynamics-book/tree/main/scripts/stress_harness).

### CDCS spine: three strata × three levels

The book organises modelling into **strata** (what kind of object we posit) and Pearl’s **levels of Reason** (what query we ask; Pearl 2009):

| | **L1 Association** | **L2 Intervention** | **L3 Counterfactual** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Structural** | Graph / dependencies | Mechanisms, $do(\cdot)$, identification | Full SCM with shared $\mathbf{u}$ |
| **Dynamical** | Forecast from history | Policies / transitions under $do(\cdot)$ | Replay trajectory with fixed $\mathbf{u}$ |
| **Observable** | Fit $P(Y \mid \cdot)$ | Estimate interventional targets from data | Infer $\mathbf{u}$, then counterfactual $Y$ |

This notebook follows that progression as an **analysis path**: structure and identification first, then time/policies, then estimation on observables (synthetics → edge stress → real cohorts), then audit. Bayesian heads appear where the stratum calls for them (Turing when $n$ is small; RxInfer when $n$ is larger).

Quarto’s Julia engine displays only the **last** value in a chunk; computation, printed summaries, and figures are split deliberately.

### Packages

| Package | Role in this notebook |
|---------|----------------------|
| [CausalDynamics.jl](https://github.com/SimonAB/CausalDynamics.jl) | Graphs, `identify`, `GraphSCM`, RxInfer bridge |
| [CausalTargeted.jl](https://github.com/SimonAB/CausalTargeted.jl) | LMTP / g-comp / sequential / survival / positivity / MTP curves |
| [CausalMediation.jl](https://github.com/SimonAB/CausalMediation.jl) | Interventional mediation grids |
| [DAGMakie.jl](https://github.com/SimonAB/DAGMakie.jl) | Causal DAG / adjustment display |
| [Turing.jl](https://github.com/TuringLang/Turing.jl) | MCMC for small-$n$ Bayesian checks |

| [TMLE.jl](https://github.com/TARGENE/TMLE.jl) | Complementary point-treatment CM / ATE (not run here) |

Literature anchors: Díaz et al. (2023) LMTP; Díaz & Hejazi (2020) mediation; van der Laan & Rose (2011); Pearl (2009); Liu et al. (2022) CircVax; Hill (2011) IHDP. Full DOIs in [references.md](https://github.com/SimonAB/CausalTargeted.jl/blob/main/docs/src/references.md).

```{julia}
#| label: chunk-setup-helpers
#| warning: false

"""Absolute path under `docs/data/`."""
data_path(name::AbstractString) = joinpath(DATA, name)

const RESULTS = DataFrame(
    section = String[],
    estimand = String[],
    expected = Float64[],
    actual = Float64[],
    abs_error = Float64[],
    cover_95 = Union{Missing, Bool}[],
    note = String[],
)

const TIMINGS = DataFrame(section = String[], seconds = Float64[])

function compare_to_truth(est, truth; se = nothing, z = 1.96)
    abs_err = abs(Float64(est) - Float64(truth))
    cover = if se === nothing || !isfinite(Float64(se))
        missing
    else
        half = z * Float64(se)
        (Float64(truth) >= Float64(est) - half) && (Float64(truth) <= Float64(est) + half)
    end
    return (; abs_err, cover, estimate = Float64(est), truth = Float64(truth))
end

function record!(section, estimand; expected, actual, se = nothing, note = "")
    c = compare_to_truth(actual, expected; se = se)
    push!(RESULTS, (
        string(section), string(estimand),
        c.truth, c.estimate, c.abs_err, c.cover, string(note),
    ))
    return c
end

"""Run `f`, push wall time into `TIMINGS`, print a one-line timing, return `f()`'s value.

Call as `timed!("label") do … end` (do-block is the first argument).
"""
function timed!(f::Function, section::AbstractString)
    t0 = time()
    out = f()
    elapsed = time() - t0
    push!(TIMINGS, (section = string(section), seconds = elapsed))
    println("⏱ ", section, ": ", round(elapsed; digits = 3), " s")
    return out
end

nothing
```

## Part I — Structural stratum

Graphs, identification certificates, and `GraphSCM` simulation. L1: dependence structure; L2: $do(\cdot)$ and backdoor identification; L3: shared exogenous $\mathbf{u}$ under alternative interventions.

### Identify, intervene, and counterfact on an SCM (L1–L3)

Association of structure (DAG), identification for intervention (`identify`), then factual vs $do(\cdot)$ under shared $U$, with Turing (small $n$) and RxInfer (larger $n$) estimating the structural slope from observational draws.

Linear confounding $Z\to X$, $Z\to Y$, $X\to Y$ with structural slope $\tau=2$ on $X\to Y$.
`simulate_scm` passes **sorted parent indices** then $U$ (see CausalDynamics `simulate_scm`), so $Y$'s equation must be `(z, x, u) -> …`, not `(x, z, u)`.
**Expected:** shared-$U$ $do(X)$ contrast $= \tau\,\Delta X$, and Bayesian $\hat\tau$ near 2.

```{julia}
#| label: chunk-scm-build
#| warning: false

g_scm = DiGraph(3)
add_edge!(g_scm, 1, 2)
add_edge!(g_scm, 1, 3)
add_edge!(g_scm, 2, 3)
# Parents of Y are sorted inneighbors [Z, X] → arguments (z, x, u).
equations = Dict{Int, Function}(
    1 => (u,) -> u,
    2 => (z, u) -> z + u,
    3 => (z, x, u) -> 2x + z + u,
)
scm = GraphSCM(g_scm, equations, Set{Int}())
id_scm = identify(g_scm, TotalEffectQuery(2, 3); node_names = Dict(1 => :Z, 2 => :X, 3 => :Y))
println("identify strategy=", id_scm.strategy, " adjustment=", id_scm.adjustment)
@assert id_scm.strategy == :backdoor
```

```{julia}
#| label: fig-scm-dag
#| warning: false
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Confounding DAG for the GraphSCM example (DAGMakie adjustment highlight)."

fig, ax, p = dagplot(g_scm;
    nlabels = ["Z", "X", "Y"],
    smart = :adjustment,
    treatment = 2,
    outcome = 3,
    adjustment = Set([1]),
)
```

```{julia}
#| label: chunk-scm-simulate
#| warning: false

rng_scm = StableRNG(7)
n_scm_small = 80
n_scm_large = 800
τ_structural = 2.0

function draw_scm_table(n; rng)
    rows = Vector{NamedTuple{(:Z, :X, :Y), Tuple{Float64, Float64, Float64}}}(undef, n)
    for i in 1:n
        U = Dict(1 => randn(rng), 2 => 0.4 * randn(rng), 3 => 0.3 * randn(rng))
        v = simulate_scm(scm, U)
        rows[i] = (Z = Float64(v[1]), X = Float64(v[2]), Y = Float64(v[3]))
    end
    return DataFrame(rows)
end

df_scm_small = timed!("scm_simulate_small_n=$(n_scm_small)") do
    draw_scm_table(n_scm_small; rng = StableRNG(71))
end
df_scm_large = timed!("scm_simulate_large_n=$(n_scm_large)") do
    draw_scm_table(n_scm_large; rng = StableRNG(72))
end

U0 = Dict(1 => 0.2, 2 => 0.1, 3 => -0.05)
v_fact = simulate_scm(scm, U0)
y_fact = v_fact[3]
x_fact = v_fact[2]
y_do = simulate_scm(apply_intervention(scm, do_intervention(2, 1.5)), U0)[3]
Δy = y_do - y_fact
Δx = 1.5 - x_fact
println("shared-U do(X=1.5) ΔY=", round(Δy; digits = 3),
    "  τ·ΔX=", round(τ_structural * Δx; digits = 3))
@assert isapprox(Δy, τ_structural * Δx; atol = 1e-10)
record!(:scm_do_shared_U, "ΔY";
    expected = τ_structural * Δx, actual = Δy,
    note = "L3 shared-U exact")
first(df_scm_small, 3)
```

```{julia}
#| label: chunk-scm-turing
#| warning: false

Turing.@model function backdoor_ate_turing(Y, X, Z)
    τ ~ Normal(0, 5)
    βz ~ Normal(0, 5)
    μ0 ~ Normal(0, 5)
    σ ~ truncated(Normal(1, 1); lower = 0.05)
    for i in eachindex(Y)
        Y[i] ~ Normal(μ0 + τ * X[i] + βz * Z[i], σ)
    end
end

chn_scm = timed!("turing_scm_small_n=$(n_scm_small)") do
    sample(
        backdoor_ate_turing(df_scm_small.Y, df_scm_small.X, df_scm_small.Z),
        NUTS(0.8),
        300;
        progress = false,
    )
end
τ_turing = mean(chn_scm[:τ])
record!(:scm_turing, "τ";
    expected = τ_structural, actual = τ_turing,
    note = "NUTS n=$n_scm_small")
println("Turing τ_mean=", round(τ_turing; digits = 3), "  structural=", τ_structural)
```

## Part II — Dynamical stratum

Time-indexed policies: sequential LMTP and discrete survival. These are L2 queries on unfolding state (then an explicit missing-data edge).

### Sequential panel (L2)

Two-wave panel with a time-varying covariate; lean / small-$n$ learners.

```{julia}
#| label: chunk-sequential
#| warning: false

rng = StableRNG(24)
n = 40
W = randn(rng, n)
A1 = 0.5 .* W .+ randn(rng, n)
L1 = 0.3 .* A1 .+ randn(rng, n)
A2 = 0.4 .* L1 .+ 0.2 .* W .+ randn(rng, n)
Y = 0.5 .* A2 .+ 0.3 .* A1 .+ 0.2 .* W .+ randn(rng, n)
df_seq = DataFrame(W = W, A1 = A1, L1 = L1, A2 = A2, Y = Y)
res_seq = timed!("sequential_lmtp_n=$n") do
    run_sequential_lmtp(
        df_seq, [:A1, :A2], :Y;
        baseline = [:W],
        time_vary = [Symbol[], [:L1]],
        delta = 0.25,
        folds = 2,
        learners = SMALL_N_SL_LEARNERS,
        rng = StableRNG(25),
    )
end
println("n=", n, " ψ≈", round(res_seq.estimate; digits = 4),
    " SE≈", round(res_seq.se; digits = 4))
record!(:sequential_tiny, "ψ(δ=0.25)";
    expected = res_seq.estimate, actual = res_seq.estimate, se = res_seq.se,
    note = "self-check finite; no oracle")
```

### Discrete survival LMTP (L2)

Event-free horizon under a modified treatment policy along a discrete-time hazard path.

```{julia}
#| label: chunk-survival
#| warning: false

df_surv, truth_surv = simulate_discrete_survival_mtp(160; rng = StableRNG(40))
shift = additive_shift_policy(; scale = "raw", lower_q = 0.0, upper_q = 1.0)
res_surv = timed!("survival_lmtp") do
    run_survival_lmtp(
        df_surv, truth_surv.treatments, truth_surv.surv;
        baseline = [:W],
        delta = 0.25,
        folds = 2,
        learners = (:glm, :mean),
        shift = shift,
        rng = StableRNG(41),
    )
end
println("ψ≈", round(res_surv.estimate; digits = 4), " SE≈", round(res_surv.se; digits = 4))
record!(:survival_lmtp, "ψ";
    expected = res_surv.estimate, actual = res_surv.estimate, se = res_surv.se,
    note = "finite self-check")
```

### Sequential panel under missing $Y$ (edge, L2)

Two-wave panel with time-varying covariate; `Missing` in $Y$ completes under `handle_missing=:drop` ([CausalTargeted#10](https://github.com/SimonAB/CausalTargeted.jl/issues/10)).

```{julia}
#| label: chunk-seq-missing
#| warning: false

rng = StableRNG(24)
n = 40
W = randn(rng, n)
A1 = 0.5 .* W .+ randn(rng, n)
L1 = 0.3 .* A1 .+ randn(rng, n)
A2 = 0.4 .* L1 .+ randn(rng, n)
Y = 0.5 .* A2 .+ 0.3 .* A1 .+ 0.2 .* W .+ randn(rng, n)
df_seq_cc = DataFrame(W = W, A1 = A1, L1 = L1, A2 = A2, Y = Y)
oracle_seq = run_sequential_lmtp(
    df_seq_cc, [:A1, :A2], :Y;
    baseline = [:W],
    time_vary = [Symbol[], [:L1]],
    delta = 0.25,
    folds = 2,
    learners = SMALL_N_SL_LEARNERS,
    rng = StableRNG(25),
)
df_seq_m = copy(df_seq_cc)
df_seq_m.Y = Vector{Union{Float64, Missing}}(df_seq_m.Y)
df_seq_m.Y[1:8] .= missing
res_seq_m = timed!("sequential_missing_drop") do
    run_sequential_lmtp(
        df_seq_m, [:A1, :A2], :Y;
        baseline = [:W],
        time_vary = [Symbol[], [:L1]],
        delta = 0.25,
        folds = 2,
        learners = SMALL_N_SL_LEARNERS,
        handle_missing = :drop,
        rng = StableRNG(25),
    )
end
println("complete-case oracle ψ≈", round(oracle_seq.estimate; digits = 4),
    "  missing-Y drop ψ≈", round(res_seq_m.estimate; digits = 4))
record!(:sequential_missing, "ψ(δ=0.25)";
    expected = oracle_seq.estimate, actual = res_seq_m.estimate, se = res_seq_m.se,
    note = "complete-case panel oracle; MAR Y dropped")
DataFrame(
    edge = ["sequential_missing"],
    detail = ["drop ok; oracle=$(round(oracle_seq.estimate; digits=4))"],
)
```

Same DAG as @fig-seq-dag-ok; only $Y$ carries `Missing`.

### Discrete survival under missing $S_T$ (edge, L2)

Terminal event-free indicator $S_T$ is MAR given $W$. Survival *censoring* IPCW (`C_1,\ldots,C_T`) is a different mechanism; this probe is missing event indicators ([CausalTargeted#10](https://github.com/SimonAB/CausalTargeted.jl/issues/10)).

Expected: `:drop` finishes without `Float64(::Missing)`; complete-data $\psi$ is the in-sample oracle; `:ipcw` should differ from `:drop` when missingness is informative.

```{julia}
#| label: chunk-surv-missing
#| warning: false

df_surv_cc = copy(df_surv)
Sh = truth_surv.surv[end]
rng_sm = StableRNG(42)
df_surv_m = copy(df_surv_cc)
df_surv_m[!, Sh] = Vector{Union{Float64, Missing}}(df_surv_m[!, Sh])
p_miss_s = 1.0 ./ (1.0 .+ exp.(-(-1.4 .+ 0.8 .* df_surv_m.W)))
for i in 1:nrow(df_surv_m)
    rand(rng_sm) < p_miss_s[i] && (df_surv_m[i, Sh] = missing)
end
ψ_surv_oracle = Float64(truth_surv.survival(0.25))
surv_miss = Dict{Symbol, NamedTuple}()
timed!("survival_missing_strategies") do
    surv_miss[:complete] = (
        est = Float64(res_surv.estimate), se = Float64(res_surv.se),
    )
    for strat in (:drop, :ipcw)
        r = run_survival_lmtp(
            df_surv_m, truth_surv.treatments, truth_surv.surv;
            baseline = [:W],
            delta = 0.25,
            folds = 2,
            learners = (:glm, :mean),
            shift = shift,
            handle_missing = strat,
            rng = StableRNG(41),
        )
        surv_miss[strat] = (est = Float64(r.estimate), se = Float64(r.se))
        record!(:survival_missing, String(strat);
            expected = ψ_surv_oracle, actual = Float64(r.estimate),
            se = Float64(r.se),
            note = "DGP survival(δ); MAR terminal S")
    end
end
surv_drop_eq = isapprox(surv_miss[:drop].est, surv_miss[:ipcw].est; atol = 1e-10)
println("miss $(Sh) rate≈", round(mean(ismissing.(df_surv_m[!, Sh])); digits = 2),
    "  DGP oracle≈", round(ψ_surv_oracle; digits = 3),
    "  complete ψ≈", round(surv_miss[:complete].est; digits = 3),
    "  drop≡ipcw? ", surv_drop_eq)
DataFrame(
    strategy = ["complete", "drop", "ipcw"],
    est = [surv_miss[s].est for s in (:complete, :drop, :ipcw)],
    se = [surv_miss[s].se for s in (:complete, :drop, :ipcw)],
)
```

```{julia}

#| warning: false
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Survival LMTP under MAR terminal $S_T$ versus complete-data and DGP oracles."

fig = Figure(size = (560, 300))
ax = Axis(fig[1, 1];
    xlabel = "handle_missing", ylabel = "ψ",
    title = "Survival, MAR terminal S",
    xticks = (1:3, ["complete", "drop", "ipcw"]),
)
ys = [surv_miss[s].est for s in (:complete, :drop, :ipcw)]
ses = [surv_miss[s].se for s in (:complete, :drop, :ipcw)]
barplot!(ax, 1:3, ys; color = (:seagreen, 0.85))
errorbars!(ax, 1:3, ys, ses; whiskerwidth = 8, color = :black)
hlines!(ax, [ψ_surv_oracle]; color = :firebrick, linestyle = :dash, label = "DGP oracle")
axislegend(ax; position = :rb)
fig
```

## Part III — Observable stratum

Estimate interventional targets from data: package synthetics (oracle recovery), edge stress, then real cohorts. Predominately L2; Bayesian heads reuse the structural / observable bridge.


### Standard synthetics (L2 recovery)

#### Linear MTP

Closed-form TE vs lean Super Learner grid.

```{julia}
#| label: chunk-linear-compute
#| warning: false

rng = StableRNG(101)
n = 200
δ = 0.5
df_lin, truth_lin = simulate_linear_mtp(n; rng = rng)
ψ_true = truth_shift_effect(truth_lin, δ)
grid_lin = timed!("lmtp_linear_n=$n") do
    run_lmtp_grid(
        df_lin, :A, :Y;
        baseline = [:W],
        deltas = [-0.5, 0.0, δ],
        folds = 2,
        learners_outcome = DEFAULT_SL_LEARNERS,
        learners_trt = DEFAULT_SL_LEARNERS,
        parallel = false,
        positivity = true,
        rng = StableRNG(102),
    )
end
row = only(filter(r -> r.delta == δ, eachrow(grid_lin)))
c = record!(:linear_mtp, "TE(δ=$δ)"; expected = ψ_true, actual = row.est, se = row.se)
println("expected=", round(ψ_true; digits = 4),
    " actual=", round(row.est; digits = 4),
    " |err|=", round(c.abs_err; digits = 4),
    " cover=", c.cover)
```

#### Continuous MTP mediation

TE / NDE / NIE under CausalMediation.

```{julia}
#| label: chunk-mediation
#| warning: false

df_med, truth_med = CausalTargeted.simulate_continuous_mtp_mediation(180; rng = StableRNG(301))
δ = 1.0
grid_med = timed!("mediation_grid") do
    CausalMediation.run_mediation_grid(
        df_med, :A, :Y;
        mediators = [:M],
        covar = [:W],
        deltas = [δ],
        folds = 2,
        n_mc = 16,
        learners = (:glm, :mean),
        parallel = false,
        rng = StableRNG(302),
    )
end
# Grid `delta` is on the same scale as `truth.effects(δ)` (z-units in this DGP).
# Do **not** pass `effective_sd_shift` into the oracle when the grid already applied δ.
ψ_oracle = truth_med.effects(δ)
for est_name in ("NDE", "NIE", "TE")
    row_e = only(filter(r -> r.estimand == est_name, eachrow(grid_med)))
    truth_v = Float64(getfield(ψ_oracle, Symbol(lowercase(est_name))))
    record!(:mediation_mtp, est_name;
        expected = truth_v, actual = Float64(row_e.est), se = Float64(row_e.se),
        note = "oracle effects(δ=$δ); lean SL")
end
println("oracle TE≈", round(ψ_oracle.te; digits = 3),
    " actual TE≈", round(only(filter(r -> r.estimand == "TE", grid_med)).est; digits = 3))
first(grid_med, min(6, nrow(grid_med)))
```

#### Weak positivity

Clamped shifts; noisy recovery by design.

```{julia}
#| warning: false

δ = 0.5

end

record!(:weak_positivity_mtp, "TE(δ=$δ)";

pos_wp = positivity_report(df_wp, :A; deltas = [0.0, δ])
println("oracle≈", round(ψ_wp; digits = 3), " est≈", round(roww.est; digits = 3))
first(pos_wp, 4)
```

#### High-cardinality site

Many rare levels; schema / fold stress.

Unseen fold levels should surface as a controlled schema / design-matrix issue.

```{julia}
#| label: chunk-high-card
#| warning: false

rng = StableRNG(88)
n = 80
W = randn(rng, n)
# many rare sites → folds may miss levels
site = [string("S", rand(rng, 1:25)) for _ in 1:n]
A = 0.5 .* W .+ randn(rng, n)
Y = 0.5 .* A .+ W .+ 0.5 .* randn(rng, n)
df_hc = DataFrame(W = W, site = site, A = A, Y = Y)
hc_ok = timed!("lmtp_high_cardinality_expect") do
    try
        run_lmtp_grid(
            df_hc, :A, :Y;
            baseline = [:W, :site],
            deltas = [0.5],
            folds = 2,
            learners_outcome = (:glm, :mean),
            parallel = false,
            rng = StableRNG(89),
        )
        "completed_without_throw"
    catch err
        string(typeof(err), ": ", first(split(sprint(showerror, err), '\n')))
    end
end
println("high-cardinality outcome: ", hc_ok)
DataFrame(edge = ["high_cardinality_site"], detail = [hc_ok])
```

#### Missing outcomes (MAR)

`handle_missing` strategies on LMTP. `:drop` and `:ipcw` should differ; IPCW should be closer to the complete-data TE when missingness is informative ([CausalTargeted#9](https://github.com/SimonAB/CausalTargeted.jl/issues/9)).

Expected: complete-data TE via `effects`; `:ipcw` ≠ `:drop`.

```{julia}
#| label: chunk-missing-y
#| warning: false

df_miss, truth_miss = CausalTargeted.simulate_missing_outcome_mtp(200; rng = StableRNG(9))
δ = 0.5
ψ_true_miss = Float64(truth_miss.effects(δ).te)
ests = Dict{Symbol, NamedTuple}()
timed!("lmtp_missing_strategies") do
    for strat in (:drop, :ipcw, :impute, :ipcw_impute)
        g = run_lmtp_grid(
            df_miss, :A, :Y;
            baseline = [:W],
            deltas = [δ],
            folds = 2,
            learners_outcome = (:glm, :mean),
            handle_missing = strat,
            parallel = false,
            rng = StableRNG(10),
        )
        ests[strat] = (est = Float64(only(g.est)), se = Float64(only(g.se)))
        record!(:missing_outcome_mtp, String(strat);
            expected = ψ_true_miss, actual = ests[strat].est, se = ests[strat].se)
    end
end
drop_eq = isapprox(ests[:drop].est, ests[:ipcw].est; atol = 1e-10)
println("miss rate≈", round(mean(ismissing.(df_miss.Y)); digits = 2),
    "  drop≡ipcw? ", drop_eq, " (expected false after CT#9)")
@assert !drop_eq
```

#### Missing outcomes, g-computation (MAR)

Same MAR-$Y$ DGP as the LMTP probe; plug-in g-computation should also apply IPCW weights ([CausalTargeted#9](https://github.com/SimonAB/CausalTargeted.jl/issues/9)).

Expected: `:ipcw` ≠ `:drop`; both finite. Compare to $\beta_A\delta$ as a scale check: g-comp clamps $A+\delta$. SEs use a **refitting** bootstrap ([CausalTargeted#13](https://github.com/SimonAB/CausalTargeted.jl/issues/13)); IPCW need not beat complete-case at this $n$.

```{julia}
#| label: chunk-gcomp-missing
#| warning: false

df_gmiss, truth_gmiss = CausalTargeted.simulate_missing_outcome_mtp(200; rng = StableRNG(9))
δ_g = 0.5
ψ_true_gmiss = Float64(truth_gmiss.effects(δ_g).te)
gcomp_miss = Dict{Symbol, NamedTuple}()
timed!("gcomp_missing_strategies") do
    for strat in (:drop, :ipcw)
        r = run_gcomp(
            df_gmiss, :A, :Y;
            covariates = [:W],
            delta = δ_g,
            folds = 2,
            learners = (:glm, :mean),
            rng = StableRNG(10),
            n_boot = 40,
            handle_missing = strat,
        )
        gcomp_miss[strat] = (est = Float64(r.estimate), se = Float64(r.se))
        record!(:gcomp_missing, String(strat);
            expected = ψ_true_gmiss, actual = Float64(r.estimate), se = Float64(r.se))
    end
end
gcomp_drop_eq = isapprox(gcomp_miss[:drop].est, gcomp_miss[:ipcw].est; atol = 1e-10)
println("g-comp miss rate≈", round(mean(ismissing.(df_gmiss.Y)); digits = 2),
    "  oracle TE≈", round(ψ_true_gmiss; digits = 3),
    "  drop≡ipcw? ", gcomp_drop_eq)
DataFrame(
    strategy = ["drop", "ipcw"],
    est = [gcomp_miss[:drop].est, gcomp_miss[:ipcw].est],
    se = [gcomp_miss[:drop].se, gcomp_miss[:ipcw].se],
)
```

#### Mediation under MAR $Y$

Binary treatment, linear mediation, MAR outcome. Uses `run_mediation_scalar` (A=0 vs A=1), not an MTP δ-grid, which would shift a binary exposure ([CausalMediation#4](https://github.com/SimonAB/CausalMediation.jl/issues/4)).

Expected: both strategies finish; `:ipcw` ≠ `:drop`. At $n=280$ with `(:glm, :mean)`, complete-data $\widehat{\mathrm{TE}}$ is already about $0.08$ low; MAR adds finite-sample noise (Wald need not cover $0.7$). IPCW need not beat `:drop` when missingness is a function of $W$ already in the outcome model. Around $n=800$ drop and IPCW match the complete-data estimate.

```{julia}
#| label: chunk-mediation-missing
#| warning: false

df_med_cc, truth_med_m = CausalMediation.simulate_mediation(280; rng = StableRNG(21))
rng_mm = StableRNG(22)
df_med_m = copy(df_med_cc)
df_med_m.Y = Vector{Union{Float64, Missing}}(df_med_m.Y)
p_miss_m = 1.0 ./ (1.0 .+ exp.(-(-1.2 .+ 0.9 .* df_med_m.W)))
for i in 1:nrow(df_med_m)
    rand(rng_mm) < p_miss_m[i] && (df_med_m.Y[i] = missing)
end
ψ_med_m = Float64(truth_med_m.te)
med_miss = Dict{Symbol, NamedTuple}()
timed!("mediation_missing_strategies") do
    for strat in (:drop, :ipcw)
        g = CausalMediation.run_mediation_scalar(
            df_med_m, :A, :Y;
            covar = [:W], mediators = [:M],
            folds = 2, n_mc = 8,
            estimator = :onestep,
            learners = (:glm, :mean),
            handle_missing = strat,
            rng = StableRNG(23),
        )
        row_te = only(g[g.effect .== "TE", :])
        med_miss[strat] = (est = Float64(row_te.estimate), se = Float64(row_te.se))
        record!(:mediation_missing, String(strat);
            expected = ψ_med_m, actual = Float64(row_te.estimate), se = Float64(row_te.se))
    end
end
med_drop_eq = isapprox(med_miss[:drop].est, med_miss[:ipcw].est; atol = 1e-10)
println("mediation miss rate≈", round(mean(ismissing.(df_med_m.Y)); digits = 2),
    "  oracle TE≈", round(ψ_med_m; digits = 3),
    "  drop≡ipcw? ", med_drop_eq)
DataFrame(
    strategy = ["drop", "ipcw"],
    est = [med_miss[:drop].est, med_miss[:ipcw].est],
    se = [med_miss[:drop].se, med_miss[:ipcw].se],
)
```

```{julia}
ax = Axis(fig[1, 1];

    title = "Mediation, MAR Y",
    xticks = (1:2, ["drop", "ipcw"]),

barplot!(ax, 1:2, ys; color = (:steelblue, 0.85))
errorbars!(ax, 1:2, ys, ses; whiskerwidth = 8, color = :black)
```

### Real cohorts and benchmarks (L2, with Bayesian heads)

#### Conservation: CircVax sheep + Turing

Small-$n$ g-computation and Turing NUTS on the published phenotype table.

Liu et al. (2022). Smoke freeze g-comp ATE ≈ $-1250$ (worms). Turing: lean Gaussian ATE on complete numeric covariates (Age coded as factor→float ranks).

```{julia}
#| label: chunk-sheep-gcomp
#| warning: false

sheep = CSV.read(data_path("sheep_vaccine_liu2022.csv"), DataFrame)
sheep_ate = timed!("gcomp_sheep_n=$(nrow(sheep))") do
    run_gcomp(
        sheep, :vaccine, :Total_Worms;
        covariates = [:Age, :Sex, :weight_kg],
        delta = 1.0,
        folds = 2,
        learners = (:glm, :mean),
        rng = StableRNG(44),
        n_boot = 20,
    )
end
actual = Float64(sheep_ate.estimate)
record!(:sheep_liu2022, "ATE(worms)";
    expected = -1250.7, actual = actual, se = sheep_ate.se, note = "harness seed=44")
println("ATE≈", round(actual; digits = 1), " SE≈", round(Float64(sheep_ate.se); digits = 1))
@assert actual < 0
```

```{julia}
#| label: fig-sheep-dag
#| warning: false
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Assumed CircVax adjustment DAG."

fig, ax, p = dagplot_confounding(
    ["Age/Sex/wt", "vaccine", "worms"];
    auto_align_labels = true,

fig
```

```{julia}
#| label: chunk-sheep-turing
#| warning: false

# Numeric design for a tiny Bayesian check
age_codes = Float64.(indexin(string.(sheep.Age), unique(string.(sheep.Age))))
sex_codes = Float64.(indexin(string.(sheep.Sex), unique(string.(sheep.Sex))))
Yw = Float64.(sheep.Total_Worms)
Aw = Float64.(sheep.vaccine)
Ww = Float64.(sheep.weight_kg)

Turing.@model function sheep_ate_model(Y, A, age, sex, wt)
    τ ~ Normal(0, 2000)
    βage ~ Normal(0, 500)
    βsex ~ Normal(0, 500)
    βwt ~ Normal(0, 50)
    μ0 ~ Normal(mean(Y), 2000)
    σ ~ truncated(Normal(std(Y), std(Y)); lower = 1.0)
    for i in eachindex(Y)
        Y[i] ~ Normal(μ0 + τ * A[i] + βage * age[i] + βsex * sex[i] + βwt * wt[i], σ)
    end
end

chn_sheep = timed!("turing_sheep_n=$(nrow(sheep))") do
    sample(sheep_ate_model(Yw, Aw, age_codes, sex_codes, Ww), NUTS(0.65), 250; progress = false)
end
τ_sheep = mean(chn_sheep[:τ])
record!(:sheep_turing, "τ";
    expected = actual, actual = τ_sheep, note = "compare to g-comp sign/magnitude")
println("Turing τ≈", round(τ_sheep; digits = 1), "  g-comp≈", round(actual; digits = 1))
```

```{julia}
#| label: fig-sheep-turing
#| warning: false
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Turing posterior for vaccine effect on worm burden (sheep)."

fig = Figure(size = (640, 280))
ax = Axis(fig[1, 1]; title = "Sheep τ (Turing)", xlabel = "τ (worms)", ylabel = "density")
density!(ax, vec(Array(chn_sheep[:τ])); color = (:darkorange, 0.55))
vlines!(ax, [actual]; color = :steelblue, linewidth = 2, label = "g-comp")
axislegend(ax; position = :rt)
```

#### IHDP NPCI + RxInfer

```{julia}
#| label: chunk-ihdp-rxinfer
#| warning: false

# Single continuous confounder proxy (x1) for a scalable variational backdoor head
g_ih = DiGraph(3)
add_edge!(g_ih, 1, 2); add_edge!(g_ih, 1, 3); add_edge!(g_ih, 2, 3)
df_ih = DataFrame(Z = Float64.(ihdp.x1), X = Float64.(ihdp.treatment), Y = Float64.(ihdp.y_factual))
rx_ih = timed!("rxinfer_ihdp_n=$(nrow(df_ih))") do
    infer_backdoor_effect(g_ih, df_ih, 2, 3;
        node_names = Dict(1 => :Z, 2 => :X, 3 => :Y), iterations = 40)
end
record!(:ihdp_rxinfer, "τ";
    expected = ψ_ite, actual = rx_ih.τ_mean, note = "VI with x1 only — approximate")
println("RxInfer τ≈", round(rx_ih.τ_mean; digits = 3), "  mean(ITE)≈", round(ψ_ite; digits = 3))
```

```{julia}
#| label: chunk-results-triage
#| warning: false

RESULTS.rel_err = map(RESULTS.expected, RESULTS.abs_error) do e, a
    den = max(abs(Float64(e)), 1e-8)
    Float64(a) / den
end
RESULTS.flag = map(eachrow(RESULTS)) do r
    note = string(r.note)
    occursin("self-check", note) && return "self-check"
    occursin("noisy by design", note) && return "edge-expected"
    occursin("degeneracy", note) && return "package-gap"
    occursin("approximate", note) && return "model-approx"
    c = r.cover_95
    if c === true || (c === missing && r.abs_error ≤ 0.05 * max(abs(r.expected), 1.0))
        return "ok"
    elseif c === false || r.rel_err > 0.25
        return "investigate"
    else
        return "borderline"
    end
end
combine(groupby(RESULTS, :flag), nrow => :n)
```

## Reading the evidence

The parts above mirror a CDCS analysis, not a random stress checklist:

1. **Structural (L1–L3)** — draw and identify the graph; settle factual and $do(\cdot)$ outcomes under shared $\mathbf{u}$; estimate the structural slope with Turing or RxInfer by scale.
2. **Dynamical (L2)** — sequential and survival policies on unfolding time; missing $Y$ / $S_T$ under `:drop` and `:ipcw`.
3. **Observable (L2)** — recover TE on synthetics, probe edges, then run the same APIs on conservation, ecology, and CI benchmarks.
4. **Audit** — freeze matrices, timings, absolute errors.

### Where estimates fail (and why)

Failures fall into distinct buckets; conflating them misleads package triage.

| Bucket | Symptom in this notebook | Root cause | Fix |
|--------|--------------------------|------------|-----|
| Formulation | SCM Bayes $\hat\tau\approx 1$ when prose claimed $\tau=2$ | `simulate_scm` passes **sorted** parents `(z,x,u)`; equation was written as `(x,z,u)` | Write equations in sorted-parent order; assert shared-$U$ $\Delta Y=\tau\Delta X$ |
| Oracle mismatch | Mediation TE “error” ~0.26 | Compared `effects(effective_sd_shift(δ))` while the grid used `deltas=[δ]` | Compare to `truth.effects(δ)` (or the row’s `effective_shift`) |
| Freeze drift | Lizards / LaLonde large \|error\| vs smoke TSV | Notebook used different `StableRNG` / `n_boot` than the harness | Align seeds with `run_functionality.jl` (seed 44) |
| Learner guard | Bt corn `(:mean,)` alone | Empty-covariate mean learner cannot identify contrasts | `run_gcomp` errors; harness uses `(:glm, :mean)` |
| Edge by design | Weak positivity misses coverage | Clamped density ratios | Keep as stress; do not treat as regression failure |
| Model approx | Sheep Turing vs g-comp; IHDP RxInfer on $x_1$ only | Different functional form / incomplete adjustment | Compare within class; widen Bayes adjustment set when claiming recovery |
| Self-check | Sequential abs_error $=0$ | `expected = actual` | Prefer complete-case or MC oracles (survival MAR now uses DGP `survival(δ)`) |
| Small-$n$ mediation MAR | TE $\approx 0.54$ vs oracle $0.7$ at $n=280$ | Lean learners; recovers with complete-data at $n\approx 800$ | Keep as stress; do not treat as IPCW wiring failure |

Linear and mixed-baseline MTP remain the clean recovery gate (small absolute error, Wald coverage). That is where the stack is strong; the failures above are mostly audit formulation, not a collapse of LMTP on its native DGPs.

That is the practical meaning of versatility here: one typed stack across strata and Pearl levels, from tens of rows (sheep, lizards) to hundreds or thousands (IHDP, SCM large draw), without leaving Julia. Where R or Python remains preferable for an existing pipeline, see the decision card in
[ECOSYSTEM_COMPARISON.md](https://github.com/SimonAB/CausalTargeted.jl/blob/main/ECOSYSTEM_COMPARISON.md).

## Open gaps

| Gap | Issue |
|-----|-------|
| Sequential Monte Carlo oracles | Notebook still uses complete-case / self-check for some dynamical rows |
| MIRS spectra, full Twins $X$, large ecology LMTP | [causal-dynamics-book#14](https://github.com/SimonAB/causal-dynamics-book/issues/14) |

Closed in this cycle: IPCW in LMTP/gcomp ([CT#9](https://github.com/SimonAB/CausalTargeted.jl/issues/9)), sequential missing `Y` under `:drop` ([CT#10](https://github.com/SimonAB/CausalTargeted.jl/issues/10)), survival MAR $S_T$ IPCW wiring, mean-only guard ([CT#11](https://github.com/SimonAB/CausalTargeted.jl/issues/11)), fold-stable mediation schema ([CT#8](https://github.com/SimonAB/CausalTargeted.jl/issues/8) / [CM#3](https://github.com/SimonAB/CausalMediation.jl/issues/3)), GraphSCM parent order ([CD#8](https://github.com/SimonAB/CausalDynamics.jl/issues/8)), g-comp refitting bootstrap ([CT#13](https://github.com/SimonAB/CausalTargeted.jl/issues/13)), mediation PPL `handle_missing` ([CM#4](https://github.com/SimonAB/CausalMediation.jl/issues/4)).
